concepts.name: volatility
concepts.definition: Volatility is the speed and range of price movement. Higher volatility requires wider, risk-aware stop and target planning.

concepts.name: trend
concepts.definition: Trend is persistent directional structure. For Atlas, trend quality is stronger when momentum and session liquidity confirm it.

concepts.name: market_structure
concepts.definition: Market structure maps sequences of highs/lows and reaction zones to identify continuation, transition, or range conditions.

concepts.name: xauusd_structure_pipeline
concepts.summary: Directional bias should come from structure first, then momentum, then location, then macro/session confirmations.

concepts.name: trend_structure
concepts.summary: Higher highs and higher lows support bullish bias. Lower highs and lower lows support bearish bias. Mixed structure implies no-trade bias.

concepts.name: momentum_quality
concepts.summary: Momentum confirms direction when candle body strength and follow-through align with structure. Weak/mixed momentum should reduce conviction.

concepts.name: location_quality
concepts.summary: Edge improves near support for buys and near resistance for sells. Middle-of-range entries usually have poor asymmetry.

concepts.name: macro_confirmation
concepts.summary: DXY and US10Y are context checks. Gold tends to benefit from DXY weakness and yield softness; conflict should reduce confidence.

concepts.name: session_quality
concepts.summary: London and London-New York overlap are usually higher quality for XAUUSD than low-liquidity sessions.

concepts.name: spread_and_liquidity
concepts.summary: Execution quality can erase edge. Wide spread/poor liquidity should block or down-rank candidates.

concepts.name: news_risk
concepts.summary: High-impact windows can invalidate otherwise good setups due to unstable volatility and slippage.

concepts.name: no_trade_is_valid
concepts.summary: No-trade is an active risk decision, not a failure. Prefer no-trade when confluence is weak or contradictory.

concepts.name: execution_boundary
concepts.summary: Analysis confidence does not authorize execution; ExecutionGate remains final authority.

concepts.name: regime_label
concepts.summary: Atlas tags each cycle with one simple observational regime label: trending, ranging, high_volatility, or low_volatility.
signals: trending: close-to-close slope exceeds the trend threshold and is strong relative to ATR proxy
ranging: slope and ATR proxy do not confirm trend or volatility extremes
high_volatility: ATR proxy exceeds the high-volatility threshold
low_volatility: ATR proxy is low and slope is muted
implications: The label is for evidence and later review only
It does not change ranking weights or execution policy automatically
Raw metrics are persisted with the label so operators can verify it against price data

concepts.name: missed_trade_review
concepts.summary: A missed trade is only a useful teaching label when Atlas had a clean playbook, aligned context, acceptable execution conditions, and still held.
implications: Do not call every hold a missed trade
Separate valid patience from excessive caution
Use too_cautious when the setup was clean but Atlas still hesitated

concepts.name: execution_friction
concepts.summary: Execution friction is the gap between a good idea and a trade that can actually be filled with acceptable cost and slippage.
implications: execution_issue is the right teaching label when the idea is recognizable but trading cost is unsafe
Do not weaken strategy rules to solve broker/spread problems
Track friction separately from setup quality

concepts.name: regime_transition
concepts.summary: Regime transition is when market behavior shifts between range, trend, and volatile expansion. Atlas should slow down until persistence is visible.
signals: trend structure begins to form after range
implications: Prefer observation or smaller confidence adjustments
Avoid labeling transition noise as a clean missed trade

core: No forced trades in proven mode
hard_filters: Block when structure is invalid or unclear
Block when reconciliation/forced-flat/safety controls require hold

london.notes: Strong directional drives and cleaner structure transitions.

overlap.notes: Highest participation and stronger momentum follow-through.

new_york.notes: News-sensitive. Moves can be strong but more event-driven.

core_concepts.market_structure: Price moves through trend, consolidation, transition, and expansion phases.
core_concepts.trend: Direction alone is insufficient; quality requires persistence and pullback behavior.
core_concepts.volatility: Volatility determines feasible stop/target distance and influences signal reliability.
core_concepts.liquidity: Liquidity affects fill quality and slippage. Thin books increase execution uncertainty.
core_concepts.momentum: Momentum is continuation pressure and is stronger when aligned with structure and liquidity.
core_concepts.support_resistance: Support/resistance are reaction probabilities, not guaranteed turn points.
core_concepts.confluence: Independent factors aligning in the same direction increase expected edge.

risk_basics.position_sizing: Risk per trade must be bounded before entry quality is considered.
risk_basics.drawdown_control: Drawdown limits protect strategy survival during adverse regimes.
risk_basics.execution_caution: Wide spreads, thin liquidity, or unstable feeds reduce expected edge.
risk_basics.quality_over_frequency: Trading less can improve expectancy when low-quality setups dominate.

bad_setup: Atlas likes a setup despite missing structure, location, or confirmation

atlas_operational_limits.grounding: Atlas answers from configured state, known rules, and validated memory.
atlas_operational_limits.no_hallucinated_edge: Atlas should not claim predictive certainty without evidence.
atlas_operational_limits.read_only_assistant: Ask Atlas is analytical and read-only unless separate command paths are invoked.
